notes: Dict key order is part of the wording. `need` stays in every request, unused by the policy, because answers move when other questions in the same request change. Every question is asked per group `i` of the batch; `pick_{i}` criteria are added by code: the group's 1-3 word spans h0..hN, then `none`.

need_{i}.instructions: Does `groups[{i}].text` contain one word or short phrase that carries the key point of the line, such as a contrast, a surprising number, a product being introduced, or a verdict, that the viewer must not miss?

criteria.true: One phrase clearly carries the line (a contrast, a count, a product being introduced, a verdict or a surprising claim) and the rest of the line is supporting words.
criteria.false: The line is setup, narration or a routine step and no phrase matters more than the rest. Most lines in a video are like this.

instructions.question: Is there exactly one word or short phrase in `groups[{i}].text` that is the point of the line, so that highlighting it would help a viewer who only skims the captions?
instructions.not_for: Lines that are setup, connective words, routine step-by-step narration, or where every part matters equally.

pick_{i}.instructions: Pick the single word or short phrase in `groups[{i}].text` that should be highlighted: the words that carry the point of the line. Prefer the shortest span that still carries it. Choose none if nothing stands out.

criteria.none: No single word or phrase stands out; nothing in this line should be highlighted.
